content:
STAGE: orientation
GOAL: fix the design direction for one in-scope idea that uses the training-only behaviour graph's OWN curvature as a design target for the RQ-VAE prefix geometry, coupled to hyperbolic computation in one path.
READ: the round prompt's evidence block (curvature study over 182 SID tables; standardised level-3 curvature +0.26/+0.34 recall correlation, level-1 -0.16, L1-L3 -0.20; raw curvature null; SID-quality R^2=0.60; issue #127 collapse-to-4-codes failure at recall 0.0513); the three prior rounds' rejected titles (Poincare-Frechet successor codebook, feedback-curvature per-level control, behaviour-ranked radial Poincare assignment).
OBSERVED: all three prior arms manipulate per-item or per-level SCALARS that weight or reshape an existing Euclidean codebook (successor-weighted Frechet means, a hard transition score mapped to per-level curvature, transition-entropy mapped to per-level radius). None of them builds the curvature of the level's quotient graph into a geometric object that the encoder and the quantizer must jointly obey, and none of them uses curvature as a MATCHING TARGET with an explicit null.
REASONING: the gap is the null-standardised curvature profile itself. Prior arms treat curvature as a per-level control knob; the evidence says the informative object is the (level-1 minus level-3) CONTRAST of the standardised quotient-graph curvature (flatter profile is better). That contrast is a signed scalar per SID table and it is measurable on the TRAINING split only, so it can be a training target while remaining a design target rather than a predictor. The idea must also answer issue #127: it must not coarsen the partition, so the target must act on the SHAPE of the prefix embedding manifold, not on the number of cells.
OPEN: whether the repo already exposes an Ollivier-curvature / quotient-graph routine I can cite (read-only check), and the exact per-step cost at 24556 items / 24 steps / 3000 epochs.

FINAL ANSWER 1/2. Idea: nullcurv-hinge-rq. Title: a size-preserving null-calibrated curvature hinge on the per-level code quotient learns the per-level curvature of a hyperbolic RQ-VAE quantizer.
Motivation: forensics show the informative object is the null-standardised quotient curvature PROFILE and its across-level SLOPE (L3 +0.26/+0.34, L1 -0.16, L1-L3 -0.20 p=0.0095; rising with depth is better; raw curvature useless, p=0.65, level-size confounded). Here that slope becomes a training-time design target and the only variables that can satisfy it are the per-level curvatures of the metric the quantizer assigns in: level 1 is pushed expander-like, level 3 clustered - the opposite direction from Issue #127 (17-cell coarse alignment -> 4 codes -> 0.0513).
Novelty: (1) per-level curvature is TRAINABLE, its gradient supplied by a hinge on the standardised curvature of the partition the quantizer actually produces - curvature is an OUTPUT of a matching problem, not a formula from a behavioural score (CURVCTRL-SID), not a per-item rank/radius (BRad-RQ), not a successor-weighted Frechet mean (round 128). (2) target is the null-standardised quantity, so the level-size confound is removed in the loop (10 membership shuffles preserving the code histogram, refreshed every 250 epochs). (3) target is a PROFILE ORDER ktilde1<=ktilde2<=ktilde3 with margin 0 = the sign boundary of the measured -0.20, not a chosen constant.
Change: Euclidean nearest-code metric replaced by a per-level Lorentz distance of trainable curvature c_l, plus one loss penalising inversions of the standardised Ollivier profile of the soft code quotient; the gradient reaches c_l only, and c_l is what selects codes, so partition and metric are optimised against each other in one path.
Behaviour: triple (ktilde1,ktilde2,ktilde3) of the training transition graph contracted into each level's code quotient. Computed from directed consecutive-pair counts on the TRAINING split only; W = n + n^T degree-normalised, 20 neighbours per row; contracted with the soft code posterior of a 1023-item training batch into B_l; Ollivier curvature of the 0.5-lazy walk with the 8 largest-mass neighbours, averaged over the top-128 edges by mass; standardised by mu,sigma of 10 size-preserving shuffles, refreshed every 250 epochs.
Leakage: W, null histogram, edge sample, epoch-0 usage all from training split and training items only; no validation/test interaction enters; SID frozen before Stage-3 test; diagnostics recorded, never gating.
Geometry: Lorentz model of curvature -c_l, c_l = 1.0*exp(eta_l) trainable (c_0 = 1.0 documented default), d_{L,c}(x,y) = (1/sqrt c) arccosh(-c<x,y>_L), exp_0/log_0 at origin, entropic W1 with ground cost d_{L,c_l}. Acts in the quantizer metric, the commitment term and the curvature estimator's ground metric; encoder/decoder/Stage-3 stay Euclidean.
Coupling path: W -> B_l(c_l) -> lazy walk -> entropic W1 in the curved metric -> khat_l -> null standardisation -> profile hinge -> dL/deta_l -> c_l -> d_{L,c_l} nearest-code search -> codes -> SID. Constant W makes the hinge identically 0 (c_l = c_0); a Euclidean ground metric makes d/dc identically 0 (baseline quantizer); only both move a geometric parameter that changes the assignment.
Coupling equation: L_curv = sum_{l=1..2}[max(0, ktilde_l - ktilde_{l+1})]^2 with ktilde_l = (mean_{E_l}[1 - W1_{d_{L,c_l}}(m_a,m_b)/d_{L,c_l}(e_{l,a},e_{l,b})] - mu_l)/max(sigma_l, 0.05|mu_l|+1e-6).
Cost at 24556 items, 1023/step, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs = 72k steps: 3 Lorentz KxK distance matrices (~6.3M MAC), 3 P^T W P products (3 x 256 x 1023 x 256 ~ 200M MAC = 0.4 GFLOP), 3 Sinkhorn blocks of 128 edges x 8x8 x 3 iters, 3 softmaxes. ~0.4 GFLOP/step = 1-3 ms on one modern GPU, +2 to +5 percent step time, +2 to 4 min over 72k steps; null refresh 12 x ~2 GFLOP < 1 min; under 2 MB extra memory; no extra encoder/decoder pass.

FINAL ANSWER 2/3 (nullcurv-hinge-rq): mechanism, safeguards, switches.
Spec: eta_l trainable clipped [-2.3,2.3]; c_l = c_0 exp(eta_l). Tangent codebook a_{l,k}; atom e_{l,k} = exp_0^{c_l}(a_{l,k}). Residual u = z - sum_{m<l} log_0^{c_m}(e_{m,k_m}); point quantised v = u/(1+||u||/10) (radial squash, r_max = 10). Selection k_l = argmin_k d_{L,c_l}(v,e_{l,k}); frozen Euclidean commitment replaced one-for-one by d^2_{L,c_l} (no new weight); decoder still consumes sum_l a_{l,k_l}, so the Stage-3 interface is untouched. Soft posterior P_l = softmax(-d/tau_l), tau_l = 1/sqrt(c_l); B_l = P_l^T W~_batch P_l symmetrised; m_a = 0.5 e_a + 0.5 B_l[a,:]/sum(B_l[a,:]); edge set = top 128 of B_l by mass; kappa = 1 - W1/d; W1 by 3-iteration log-domain Sinkhorn with eps = 0.05*mean(d) (measured scale); L = L_RQ + lambda*L_curv, lambda = L_RQ(step0)/max(L_curv(step0),1e-6) measured once (loss balancing, not a sweep).
Inputs/outputs: batch of encoder outputs (1023 x d), W~ block, tangent codebooks (3x256xd), eta (3,), cached mu/sigma; returns c_l, soft posteriors and hard SID, L_curv and dL/deta (3,), refreshed null on the 250-epoch boundary, logged profile and usage counts.
Safeguards: arccosh argument clamped [1+1e-6, 1e6]; Lorentz inner product clamped; c_l floored 1e-3; tau_l floored 1e-3; W1 normaliser floored 1e-6 and edges below 1e-6 of max B mass dropped so coincident codes cannot give infinite curvature; Sinkhorn in log domain, 3 fixed iterations; sigma_l floored at 0.05|mu_l|+1e-6 so a near-pure level-3 partition cannot make ktilde explode; deterministic top-128 edge selection (reproducible without a seed sweep); non-finite L_curv zeroes that step's curvature gradient and increments a reported counter; usage guard freezes eta_l for 100 epochs whenever a level's used-code count falls below 0.9x its epoch-0 value (explicit defence against #127); K never reduced, no code merged.
Observables: eta_l and c_l over training; hard-SID standardised profile at each null refresh; both hinge terms; used-code counts and collision rate per level; existing prefix behaviour-predictability/adjacency diagnostics; Stage-3 test_recall@10. Expected: hinge terms fall, eta_1 negative and/or eta_3 positive (rising profile), level-1 usage holds or rises, level-3 usage holds, recall above baseline.
Behaviour off: W~ replaced by a constant matrix of the same density (retained weights = 1), so B_l is level-independent up to atom geometry, hinge arguments equal, L_curv identically 0, eta stays 0, c_l = c_0 = 1; curved quantizer stays fully active, isolating the behavioural target.
Geometry off: d_{L,c_l} -> Euclidean, exp_0/log_0 -> identity, W1 with Euclidean ground cost, so dL/deta = 0 and c_l inert; reduces to the frozen Euclidean quantizer with behaviour curvature computed but unable to act.
Both on: training-split W~, size-preserving null, profile hinge, trainable per-level Lorentz curvature in code selection. No arm trained this round; all constants derived or documented (c_0 = 1.0, tau = 1/sqrt c, 20 neighbours, 3 Sinkhorn iterations, top-128 edges, R = 10, 250-epoch null period, lambda from step-0 balance).

FINAL ANSWER 3/3 (nullcurv-hinge-rq): hypothesis and risks.
Hypothesis (worth keeping only if all three hold in the single run): (a) |eta_l| >= 0.05 for at least one level by epoch 3000, proving the behaviour term reached the geometry rather than being absorbed elsewhere; (b) the hard-SID standardised profile becomes non-decreasing (both hinge terms < 0.05 at the final null refresh) while the level-3 used-code count stays >= 0.9x its epoch-0 value, i.e. the target was met without trading resolution away; (c) Stage-3 test_recall@10 > 0.065.
Risks: (1) the differentiable curvature surrogate may be dominated by the temperature and the sampled edge set rather than by the partition, so eta_l drifts for reasons unrelated to behaviour ((a) passes while (c) fails); (2) the target is measured on the level-l CODE-MARGINAL quotient (K nodes) rather than the forensic prefix-tuple quotient (up to K^l nodes) because a per-step null over prefix tuples is outside the step budget, and the marginal may have the opposite slope on some tables; (3) arccosh gradients blow up when two codes coincide, exactly the #127 collapse mode, and the radial squash, tau floor and usage guard may not be enough; (4) at level 3 the near-pure partition gives a near-zero shuffle sigma, so ktilde explodes and hijacks the loss; the sigma floor mitigates but weakens the signal; (5) with one run and no ablation, a null result cannot separate "the slope target is wrong" from "the surrogate gradient is bad", and that ambiguity must be reported rather than resolved.
Note on the round's open questions: this answers (a) by making the curvature profile a matching target inside the quantizer rather than a post-hoc predictor, and (b) by letting the standardised profile enter the LAYER-WISE geometry as per-level trainable Lorentz curvature that changes both the assignment distances and the encoder gradient. The measured #127 risk is answered by pushing level 1 toward expander-like rather than coarser, and by a usage guard keyed to the epoch-0 used-code count.
